At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
 As a Data Scientist on the Mapping team, you will collaborate with our world class team of scientists, engineers, product managers, and designers to grow and improve the quality of recommended routes and accuracy of our travel time estimations. We're looking for a passionate, driven Data Scientist who is excited to dive into our geospatial, behavioural and mobility data, and build a best-in-class mapping product that provides safe, efficient, and seamless navigation for our rideshare drivers.
 Data Science is at the heart of Lyft’s products and decision-making. You will leverage data and rigorous, analytical thinking to shape our mapping products and make business decisions that put our customers first. The Mapping team serves models and systems that determine the most efficient routes, fastest travel estimates and process real-time map data signals to detect traffic, closures and slowdowns. Working with our business and analytics partners, the team owns tools to ensure Lyft offers routes that our users trust. This will involve identifying and scoping opportunities, recommending technical solutions, designing experiments, and measuring the impact of new features. You will help us solve some of the most impactful problems in Mapping, including:
 How do we accurately predict acute and chronic traffic conditions?
 How do we improve the recommendations of our routing algorithms?
 How do we keep our travel estimation promises to our riders and drivers?
 How do we benchmark and measure the success of our services?
 Responsibilities:
 Own the complete lifecycle of algorithmic solutions from problem formulation, data exploration, and feature engineering to deployment, monitoring, and iteration
 Prioritize and lead deep dives into our data to uncover new product and business opportunities
 Partner closely with Engineering to build and scale production-grade ML systems, real-time inference services, batch pipelines, and feature stores
 Design, implement, and analyze different types of experiments, and facilitate and foster data-driven and informed decision making and prioritization
 Drive scientific excellence by introducing modern techniques in ML, optimization, reinforcement learning, or graph-based methods to unlock new product capabilities
 Establish metrics that measure the health of our products, as well as rider and driver experience
 Translate complex business challenges into concrete algorithmic solutions in close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Science teams
 Experience:
 Advanced degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, physics, economics, operations research, neuroscience, or engineering, or relevant work experience
 3+ years hands-on experience in a data science or machine learning role working with production machine learning models and optimization systems
 Passion for solving unstructured and non-standard mathematical problems
 Experience independently driving multi-project algorithmic scopes and navigating technical ambiguity from ideation to delivery
 Experience with machine learning models in production, making practical tradeoffs among algorithm sophistication, compute complexity, maintainability, and extensibility in production environments
 Strong oral and written communication skills, and ability to collaborate with and influence cross-functional partners 
 Working knowledge of modern machine learning frameworks and distributed computing systems, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Ray, Spark, etc.
 Benefits: 
 Extended health and dental coverage options, along with life insurance and disability benefits
 Mental health benefits
 Family building benefits
 Child care and pet benefits
 Access to a Lyft funded Health Care Savings Account
 RRSP plan with company match to help save for your future

Then this role may be for you! We’re looking for a Success Enablement Manager to be part of our Success Enablement team.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be. The way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011, but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ahVf4AjYlh4.

 

The Team:

The Enablement team is a central function within Jobber’s Customer Success organization, supporting the growth and performance of Product Support and Customer Onboarding. As a Center of Excellence, Enablement owns the programs, playbooks, tools, and measurement frameworks that drive operational excellence and skill development across these teams. We work cross-functionally to ensure that every team member, regardless of channel or customer type, has the knowledge, confidence, and support to deliver value. That value is measured in outcomes: customers who activate faster, stay longer, and get more out of the product.

The Role:

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Success Enablement, the Success Enablement Manager will give our Product Support and Customer Onboarding teams the information, content, and tools they need to operate more effectively.

You will own enablement end to end for both teams. That means building how specialists ramp, how they stay current as the product changes, how they access the right answer in the moment, and how they keep improving once they are proficient. It also means raising the ceiling on what those conversations deliver. An onboarding session that activates a business on the features it actually needs, and a high-quality support interaction that also surfaces a product or feature the customer is missing, are both revenue moments. Service quality comes first in both. A specialist who has not solved the problem in front of them has not earned the next conversation. Your job is to make that judgement teachable, repeatable, and measurable.

You will build the needs discovery and product positioning frameworks specialists use live, enable the Next Best Action recommendations that surface in their workspace, and partner closely with our frontline manager group to help them hit their KPIs across service levels, quality, activation, adoption, and retention.

The Success Enablement Manager will:

 - Own the enablement lifecycle for Product Support and Customer Onboarding, from new hire ramp and certification through continuous development for tenured specialists.

 - Build and maintain the needs discovery and positioning frameworks specialists use in live customer conversations, so the right product reaches the right customer at the right moment.

Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik/, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future.

We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you!

 


THE ROLE

In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include:

 - Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.

 - Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).

 - Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!

 - Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.

 - Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.

 - You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.

 - If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!

 


THE QUALIFICATIONS

We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

 - You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.

 - You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.

 - You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.

 - You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team.

 - You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.

 - You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.

 


WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

 


WHY YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY

 - You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.

 - You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.

 - You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).

 - You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

 - To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.

 - You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.

 


ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 


MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 


COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

Chez UTILE, le rôle d' agent·e de location va bien au-delà de la signature de contrats traditionnels : c'est l'occasion de contribuer concrètement à l'accès à des milieux de vie abordables pour la population étudiante et de transformer le logement au Québec.
 En tant que premier point de contact avec nos futur·es résident·es, tu auras la responsabilité d'offrir une expérience d'accueil humaine et fluide, de piloter avec rigueur le traitement des candidatures et d'assurer le succès des mises en location de nos projets.
 Ce rôle arrive à un moment stratégique : avec plus de 1 000 appartements actuellement en opération et plus de 1 700 logements en développement, tu seras au cœur de l'action pour soutenir notre croissance rapide et faire rayonner notre mission.

 Chez UTILE, tu ne fais pas que louer des logements, tu contribues à ouvrir les portes de véritables milieux de vie pour les étudiant·es : abordables, durables et humains. Et pour que tu puisses donner le meilleur de toi-même, on t'offre des conditions qui font une vraie différence :
 Poste permanent à temps plein (40 h/semaine).
 Programme de bonification.
 Minimum 4 semaines de vacances par année.
 5 congés personnels et 11 jours fériés payés.
 Assurances collectives complètes dès l'embauche.
 Cotisation de l'employeur au régime de retraite (5%) dès l'embauche.
 Ordinateur et téléphone fournis ou remboursés.
 Soutien en ergonomie de travail.
 Un Comité COOL (dédié à créer beaucoup de fun!).
 Tes responsabilités au quotidien 
 Sous la supervision de la Direction adjointe – location et administration, tu es la personne de référence pour le parcours de sélection et d'intégration des locataires. Concrètement, tes responsabilités s'articulent autour de ces grands piliers :
 Gestion et traitement des candidatures : Réceptionner les demandes de location, vérifier rigoureusement les pièces justificatives et assurer un suivi personnalisé et proactif auprès des candidat·es.
 Mise en valeur et location des logements : Gérer efficacement la mise en marché des unités vacantes (diffusion des annonces, suivi des disponibilités, tenue à jour des inventaires) à même notre CRM et les logiciels de gestion.
 Préparation et conformité des baux : Rédiger avec exactitude les baux résidentiels, leurs annexes et les avis afférents (renouvellements, modifications) prêts pour la signature officielle par les gestionnaires d’immeubles (GI).
 Coordination sur le terrain : Planifier et orchestrer avec les candidat·es et les gestionnaires d’immeubles les visites de logements ainsi que les rendez-vous de signatures.
 Soutien administratif et expérience locataire : Assurer la tenue ordonnée des dossiers locataires, effectuer le classement et offrir un service à la clientèle irréprochable et chaleureux tout au long du cycle de location.
 Ton profil pour réussir dans ce rôle 
 Pour relever ce défi et maintenir le rythme de notre croissance avec rigueur, nous cherchons une personne autonome, organisée et animée par les relations humaines.

 Connaissances locatives : Bonne compréhension du bail résidentiel et des normes applicables au Québec (Tribunal administratif du logement – TAL).
 Compétences linguistiques : Excellente maîtrise du français et de l'anglais (oral et écrit) pour interagir aisément avec notre clientèle étudiante diversifiée.
 Outils et administration : Grande aisance avec les outils bureautiques (Suite Office), la gestion de bases de données et les logiciels de gestion immobilière/locative.
 Savoir-être : Sens du détail aiguisé, structure, proactivité et capacité à coordonner plusieurs dossiers en parallèle dans le respect des échéanciers.
 Approche : Service à la clientèle exemplaire, grand entregent, empathie et facilité à créer un lien de confiance.
 On veut absolument te rencontrer si, en plus, tu as (atouts) : 
 De l’expérience concrète dans un poste d’agent·e de location ou en service à la clientèle dans le milieu de l'habitation.
 Une maîtrise du logiciel Hopem ou d’un logiciel similaire de gestion immobilière.
 Un intérêt marqué ou une expérience dans le secteur de l'économie sociale ou du logement communautaire.
 Chez UTILE, nous croyons que des équipes diversifiées renforcent nos milieux de vie : nous encourageons chaleureusement les personnes issues de groupes historiquement sous-représentés, notamment les personnes autochtones, racisées, en situation de handicap, issues de la diversité sexuelle et de genre ou ayant des parcours atypiques, à soumettre leur candidature, même si elles ne répondent pas à 100 % des critères affichés. À compétence égale, nous accordons une priorité aux candidatures issues de ces groupes et adapterons notre environnement de travail à vos besoins.

 Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : EDC offre un régime de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux concurrentiel, une bonne conciliation travail-vie personnelle et la chance de contribuer à bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce.

 As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator for Sales Development, you'll be embedded with the Sales Development (SD) team. You'll work directly with SD reps, managers, and leadership to understand how the team works, and you'll build the AI tools and automations that make that work faster and better. Your measure of success is the improvement in the speed and quality of the SD team’s work that your builds drive.
 Responsibilities
 Identify the highest-leverage workflows in SD's day-to-day work by deeply understanding the processes, inputs, and outputs behind them
 Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to how SD works
 Work with SD leaders to prioritize what to build, and be clear about what is and isn't worth building
 Ship quickly, put working versions in front of users, and improve them based on how the team uses them
 Make what you build reliable: understandable, documented, and maintainable as data, systems, and processes change
 Measure the effect of what you ship, using before-and-after evidence on time saved, quality, or work made possible
 Partner with engineering, analytics, and operations teams when a tool needs production systems, sensitive data, or long-term ownership
 Share results with SD leadership and the wider FDA team
 Who you are
 We're looking for people who have already used AI to change how real work gets done.
 You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You've built things that other people used, or that ran in production systems, and that measurably improved the speed or quality of their work.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences

 Experience taking a prototype to something reliable, such as monitoring, documentation, or handoff to an engineering owner

1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



We're hiring a Senior Manager, Infrastructure Security to lead the team responsible for securing 1Password's cloud-native platform. Reporting into Platform Security, you'll set the direction for Infrastructure Security, establish priorities, and drive execution aligned with our broader security strategy.

We're looking for a hands-on engineering leader who combines deep technical expertise with strong judgment and people leadership. You'll help your team tackle complex security challenges, prioritize work that meaningfully reduces risk, and build strong partnerships with engineering teams to make security an integral part of how our platform evolves.

Your team is responsible for security across cloud infrastructure, identity and access management, privileged access, networks, containers, and emerging AI and automated systems. You'll lead and develop a team of security engineers while partnering closely with Platform Security, Threat Operations, and infrastructure engineering leaders to strengthen our security posture.

As AI and agentic technologies become increasingly integrated into production environments, you'll also help define how we secure these systems, including their identities, access to infrastructure and data, and the controls that limit potential risk.

In this role, you'll help ensure 1Password's infrastructure remains secure, resilient, and scalable while enabling engineering teams to move quickly and confidently.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

We're looking for someone who brings strong technical depth, direct people leadership experience, and the ability to turn a security strategy into shipped work.

 - 8+ years of experience in security engineering, including at least 3 years directly managing a team, with demonstrated accountability for team delivery, individual performance, engagement, and professional growth.

 - Deep production experience securing a major cloud platform, including identity and trust boundaries, workload isolation, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code.

 - Experience building or improving privileged access programs, including how people and workloads access the systems and resources they need.

 - Experience implementing network segmentation, WAF, and zero-trust approaches at scale.

 - Hands-on experience securing AI and agentic systems in production, including workload identities, access to infrastructure and data, and security boundaries designed to limit the impact of a compromised agent.

 - Demonstrated ability to review technical work, identify gaps, and raise the quality of engineering outcomes through effective technical oversight and coaching.

 - Ability to navigate ambiguous, complex problems, establish priorities within an area of ownership, and define technical direction without relying on prescribed solutions.

 - Proven ability to influence engineering teams through technical credibility, a track record of delivering results, and the development of high-performing engineers.

 - Experience using AI to improve individual and team effectiveness, modeling responsible adoption, and ensuring AI-assisted work is reviewed for accuracy, sound judgment, and impact.
   
   

What you can expect:

 - Set the strategic direction and priorities for Infrastructure Security, and own delivery end to end, aligned with the Platform Security strategy

 - Define clear goals and metrics so progress is measurable and trade-offs can be argued with evidence

 - Lead delivery across concurrent workstreams in cloud security, identity and access management, and container security

 - Build, coach, and grow a team of security engineers: set clear expectations for what good looks like, and address both strong performance and off-track performance early rather than waiting for issues to surface

 - Work closely with platform and infrastructure engineering teams so security is designed into systems from the start

 - Help define how we secure AI and automated systems, including the identities they run as, how their access is scoped, and where the boundaries around them sit

 - Partner with the other Platform Security teams and with Threat Operations so findings reach the right owner and get remediated inside an agreed SLA

 - Make the calls Infrastructure Security needs, and bring in your peers and manager on decisions that reach beyond the team

 - Make sure security keeps up with company growth without slowing teams down







USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $230,000 USD and $334,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $202,000 CAD and $293,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.


Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What we offer

Health and wellbeing

 Growth and future

Community

🌎 Remote-first work environment

 Huawei Canada's Advanced Optical Technology Lab focuses on advanced R&D in high-performance optical communications and networking. Our expert team specializes in transmission algorithms, systems, physics, and AI-driven optical network management. The lab engages in projects ranging from deep research to developing key product features, actively participating in standards organizations and collaborative research with partners.  Modeling of end-to-end non-coherent optical transmission system. 
 Modeling of Hollow-Core Fiber and the impact of gas absorption on the transmission. 
 Exploring efficient signaling and equalization to combat channel induced fading profiles. 
 Studying the impact of high launch power on the system reach and performance.

 About the ideal candidate: 
 Currently enrolled in Master’s/PhD program in Electrical Engineering program or equivalent. 
 Solid background in non-coherent optical fiber transmission and reception. 
 Deep understanding of direct-detection systems, transceiver limitations, and noise penalties (e.g., RIN, thermal noise, shot noise). 
 Familiarity with programming languages like Matlab and/or Python. 
 Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a team. 
 A publication record on similar topics is an asset.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

About the role 

We're hiring a Chief of Staff to keep Cohere's AI organization running at full speed. You'll report to and support the Chief AI Officer and work to bridge across all teams and functions at Cohere (including research, modelling, product, delivery, security, sales and operations). In any given quarter, the org ships new AI product releases and demos, customer pilots and scaled solutions, security updates, often across regions and time zones. Your job is to make sure the right work priorities win when everything feels urgent, that our plans turn into high-quality shipped work, and that our Chief AI Officer can focus on leading instead of firefighting.

Much of this is operational: the planning calendar, the budget, the headcount plan, the weekly business reviews, the communication strategy (internal and external), the cross-functional handoffs.  Your role is the operating rhythm of the org: meetings, priorities, plans, and the decisions that come out of them.  You will be a member of an experienced, high-performing and supportive leadership team.


What you'll own 

Own the operating rhythm and planning: annual and quarterly planning, goal-setting, and the weekly and monthly business reviews. Drive budget and headcount planning against the slate, and keep both honest as priorities shift mid-quarter.

Keep major programs from colliding or stalling across research, modelling, product, delivery, and security.  Be the person teams come to when it isn't clear who owns a decision, or how to navigate trade-offs.

Be the connective tissue between the Chief AI Officer’s org and the rest of the company: cross-functional planning with product, engineering, security, and finance, so the org's commitments are realistic and its dependencies are visible.

Own and lead special projects: Lead the things that don't fit neatly on any one team's plate: a reorg, a new partnership, a flagship research event, an org-wide planning week. Own them end to end.


Who you are 

You have 12+ years of operating experience, with real time inside an AI/ML organization in a Chief of Staff, business operations, or senior program-operations seat.  You know how to partner with teams shipping fast & often to high-stakes organizations, and you know how to change course with agility when needed.

You understand how AI actually works—at the level of someone who's done it rather than managed it from a distance. You can talk credibly about how a model turns into a product, what data requirements demand from both research and engineering, and where delivery motions usually break. You're fluent in the numbers. Model performance metrics, data pipeline throughput, budget-to-impact.  You don't have to run every program yourself. You do have to understand them well enough that the people who run them respect your judgment.

You hold strategy and execution in the same hand. You can sit in a planning conversation with the Chief AI Officer in the morning and chase down a stuck deliverable in the afternoon.

You thrive in a fast-paced environment, you handle ambiguity with curiosity and confidence, you stay calm when it's messy.  You have a track record of bringing order to a fast, complex org without grinding it to a halt.

You are an outstanding communicator and know how to wield soft power. Clear writing, straight talk, the ability to influence teams and individuals, and the executive presence to represent the Chief AI Officer in high-stakes conversations.

About Us: 
 At Reusables, we’re driven by a vision of a waste-free world and recognize the urgent need to address the environmental impact of our current systems and habits. We believe that meaningful change requires institutions to offer frictionless systems that make sustainability effortless and tangible. 
 What began as a grassroots initiative offering reusable takeout containers to restaurants and cafes in Vancouver, has since grown into an enterprise technology platform reaching institutions across North America. Today, Reusables is helping to eliminate thousands of tonnes of single-use waste each year, empowering businesses to join the journey toward a cleaner, more sustainable future. 
 As a venture-backed and mission-driven company, we are passionate about making impact at scale. We are a young, weirdly talented group of ‘high-octane’ individuals that are relentlessly focused on the planet, people, and profit – in that order. 
 About the Role: 
 You'll own everything outside our door: getting the right parts to our floor at the right cost and time, and getting finished units across borders and onto campuses. That covers sourcing and procurement from suppliers in North America and Asia, inbound and outbound logistics, customs and tariffs. 
 You'll be our first dedicated supply chain hire, so you’ll get to design the end-to-end supply chain that best fits our products and demand cycles, and watch it become a core part of how Reusables runs. Very little of what we do has been done before, so most of what you set up will be one of a kind. Until our Production Manager starts, you'll also cover inventory planning and make sure the floor has what it needs. This is a full-time, permanent position to start in January 2027. 
 Our hardware is designed, built, tested and shipped by a small team in Vancouver, and you’ll report to our Hardware Lead. Most units ship in a summer peak, ahead of each autumn semester. 
 We’re moving from build-to-order to levelled production. From February we build steadily towards the September peak, and servicing and refurbishing units already in the field runs alongside new builds. 
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Buy components and purchased units, from electronic and mechanical parts to tablets, displays and enclosures, at the right cost and lead time 
 Be the main contact for our suppliers: negotiate price, MOQs and lead times, track delivery performance and resolve quality issues 
 Own supplier, cost, lead time and MOQ for every part, and bring lower-cost or more available substitutes to engineering for approval 
 Find single-source and long-lead parts, and qualify second sources before they become shortages 
 Turn the production plan and sales pipeline into a forecast, and set reorder points 
 Order ahead of factory shutdowns such as Chinese New Year 
 Arrange inbound freight and outbound shipments to customers in Canada and the US: carriers, rates, tracking and delivery dates 
 Handle HTS classification, country of origin, CUSMA documentation, duties and tariff exposure, working with our customs broker 
 Design and source packaging that protects the product and keeps freight costs down 
 Set the packing specs our production floor follows 
 Set up the inventory and BOM data and tools we need as we grow 
 Report on spend, landed cost per unit, supplier on-time delivery and inventory value 
 How Your Year Looks: 
 January to February: Take over the costed BOM and supplier list, and get orders for the build-ahead and summer peak placed before the Chinese New Year shutdown 
 February to May: Keep parts flowing for levelled production, qualify second sources, and cover inventory planning until our Production Manager is in place 
 June to September: Outbound shipping to campuses in Canada and the US, customs clearance, and chasing anything late 
 October to December: Post-season review of landed cost and supplier performance, and next year's forecast and ordering plan 
 What You’ll Bring To The Team: 
 4+ years in procurement or supply chain at a hardware or electronics manufacturer 
 Experience sourcing electronic and mechanical components, including from suppliers in Asia 
 Working knowledge of Canada–US import and export: HTS codes, CUSMA, tariffs and customs brokers 
 Enough technical depth to read a BOM and a drawing and judge whether a substitute part is a real fit 
 Strong spreadsheet skills and experience with an ERP, MRP or inventory system 
 A strong negotiator who follows through on the details 
 Eligible to work in Canada, and able to work on-site in Vancouver 
 A positive, go-getter attitude: you’re excited by a new challenge every day, and you’ll figure out what you don’t know yet 
 Self-motivated and high ownership: give you a problem and you’ll own it through to the end, without waiting to be told how 
 No ego: we’re focused on the mission and check our egos at the door 
 Nice to have 
 Experience building a supply chain function at a startup 
 APICS CPIM or CSCP, or SCMP designation 
 Experience with PCB assembly houses or contract manufacturers 
 Experience planning inventory for seasonal demand 
 If your background doesn’t perfectly align with the qualifications listed, but you’re confident in your ability to excel in this role, we still want to hear from you! At Reusables, we value diverse experiences and unique perspectives, so don’t hesitate to apply if you believe you can make a meaningful impact. We hire for attitude first. Skills can be taught, so we’d rather meet someone who takes on any task with excitement and figures it out, than someone held back by what they’ve done before. 
 We sincerely appreciate the time and effort of all applicants who express interest in joining our team. While we carefully review each application, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you for considering Reusables as your next career opportunity! 
 Compensation & Key Criteria
 Please note: This is an in-office position at our office in Vancouver, BC. 
 Compensation: $90,000-110,000 CAD per year 
 Start date: January 2027 
 Reports to: Hardware Lead 
 Why You’ll Love Working At Reusables: 
 Benefits package (dental, vision, health) 
 Membership to Outdoor Prolink for discounted outdoor gear 
 A small, fun, low-ego team that loves the work we do together and the impact we have 
 A central, spacious and easy-access office in Vancouver with a friendly, sociable atmosphere and plenty of space to focus 
 Annual offsite with the entire Reusables team 
 Work that ships: what you build, buy or plan ends up on campuses where people use it every day 
 Our Values: 
 Strive for excellence 
 Assume you have something to learn from everyone 
 Play bigger 
 Check your ego at the door 
 See the path forward, not the trees in the way 
 Why Join Us: 
 The ocean already contains 165 million tonnes of plastic, and by 2050, plastic waste could outweigh fish. While recycling is often touted as the solution, only 5% of plastic is actually recycled in the U.S. (9% in Canada). Governments and businesses worldwide are banning single-use plastics and committing to zero-waste solutions by 2030. 
 Reusable packaging is the most sustainable alternative, but adoption has been hindered by cost and operational complexity. Reusables removes these barriers, offering a scalable, tech-enabled solution for food businesses and the institutions that serve them.
